organizations.nameVariants: Carl Lindström A.-G.; Carl Lindström Aktiengesellschaft; Lindström
organizations.publicNote: German record-manufacturing company. Odeon and Parlophon/Parlophone are represented separately as recording labels rather than as variant corporate names.
Recording label within the Lindström group. Export issues used the spelling Parlophone; the label is kept distinct from the corporate body Carl Lindström AG.

sources.shortCitation: Parlophone 80.235, “Was macht jede Nacht so ein kleines Baby in der Bar”
sources.fullCitation: Saxophon Orchester Dobbri, vocal by Max Mensing. “Was macht jede Nacht so ein kleines Baby in der Bar.” Slow fox; label credit “Fritz Rotter & Dr. B. Kaper”. Parlophone 80.235, matrix B 38451, n.d. Shellac disc, Radiomuseum Hardthausen / Schallarchiv; filmed-label transfer on YouTube.
sources.title: Was macht jede Nacht so ein kleines Baby in der Bar — Parlophone 80.235
sources.creator: Saxophon Orchester Dobbri, mit Gesang: Max Mensing
sources.researchNote: The filmed label identifies Parlophone 80.235, matrix B 38451, Saxophon Orchester Dobbri and Max Mensing. R. Pfau’s Lexikon der deutschen Tanzmusik, part 8, printed p. 926, independently lists this song with “B 38451 Dobbri Saxophon Orch.” Its general year 1930 does not specify a session or issue date. The Berlin session in 1930 and the description of the copy as a French issue remain uploader-supplied; neither is printed on the label.

additionalLinks.label: R. Pfau, Lexikon der deutschen Tanzmusik, part 8, p. 926

sources.fullCitation: Orchestra Mascotte. “Moonlight at Sanssouci.” Waltz; label credit “Rotter–Kaper”. Parlophone A3436, matrix Be 9615, n.d. Australian pressing, labelled “Made in Australia for Parlophone Co. Ltd.” Disc label photograph and digital transfer published by the Great 78 Project, Internet Archive.
sources.title: Moonlight at Sanssouci — Parlophone A3436
sources.creator: Orchestra Mascotte
sources.researchNote: The Internet Archive item includes a photograph of the disc, not audio alone. The label identifies Orchestra Mascotte, Parlophone A3436 and Australia; the runout shows Be 9615, also transcribed in the item metadata. The patent dates printed around the label rim are not recording or issue dates. No independently documented issue date has been established for this Australian pressing; dates assigned to other Parlophone issues are not transferred to A3436. Orchestra Mascotte is a house name and does not identify the individual players.

additionalLinks.label: Great 78 Project — photograph of the Australian Parlophone A3436 label

sources.shortCitation: Parlophone AR 206, “Love Is a Fairy Tale”
sources.fullCitation: Richard Tauber, tenor, with orchestra conducted by Paul Dessau. “Love Is a Fairy Tale”, from The Right to Happiness; label credit “Kaper–Jurmann–Rotter”. Sung in German. Parlophone AR 206, matrix Be 9887, n.d. Australian pressing, labelled “Made in Australia for Parlophone Co. Ltd.” Disc label photograph and audio transfer published by the Great 78 Project, Internet Archive.
sources.title: Love Is a Fairy Tale — Parlophone AR 206
sources.creator: Richard Tauber, tenor, with orchestra
sources.researchNote: The Internet Archive item includes a photograph of the Australian Parlophone AR 206 label. It names Richard Tauber and conductor Paul Dessau, prints matrix Be 9887 and explicitly states “Sung in German”, despite the English song and film titles. The runout identifies take 2. The item links the reverse side as “Once There Was a Baby”. No issue date is printed or supplied in the item metadata. The earlier year 1932 and the date of the German recording session do not establish when this Australian pressing was issued; its issue date remains unknown. Patent dates around the rim are not issue dates.

additionalLinks.label: Great 78 Project — photograph of the disc label
